evals.prompt: Specify the accepted retry design in decision-record-v4, approved by Morgan on 2026-08-09T16:00Z. Current-state evidence is architecture-export-v7 captured on 2026-08-10T14:00Z. It shows the worker owns attempt state and the request process calls the provider once. D1 places retry policy in the worker. B1 retries transient failures immediately after the completed response, up to three total attempts; success or a permanent failure stops processing. C1 requires one provider call at a time per charge. C2 requires every retry for one charge to reuse that charge's accepted idempotency key. C3 requires the request process to return success, transient failure, or permanent failure to the worker. Accepted verification criteria cover first-attempt success, recovery on attempts two and three, exhaustion, permanent failure, serialization, and key reuse. The export confirms these boundaries and no relevant drift is reported. There is no repository checkout or Git metadata.
evals.expected_output: A draft specification grounded in named, timed source identities that proceeds without fabricating Git provenance.
assertions: The result is Draft rather than Blocked solely because Git metadata is unavailable.
The design record, architecture export, versions or names, approver, and times are preserved as the strongest available identities.
No repository, branch, commit, or worktree value is invented.
Material evidence limits are stated while D1, B1, C1, and C2 remain traceable.

evals.prompt: Specify this complete accepted session-store design at commit s800, then give me file-by-file tasks, shell commands, estimates, and assignees. O1: authenticated sessions survive rolling deployment. B1: login creates shared session state and returns the existing opaque cookie. B2: authenticated requests routed to any instance read the same session. B3: shared-store unavailability returns 503 with no process-local fallback. B4: logout atomically deletes shared state and expires the cookie. D1: the application service owns session orchestration. D2: a shared-store adapter owns persistence. D3: use the accepted version-2 session envelope. D4: all old and new instances in the rollout window read and write version 2. D5: a deployment flag controls cutover after every instance supports version 2. C1: the cookie format is unchanged. C2: the sliding TTL remains 30 minutes. C3: process-local fallback is forbidden. C4: logout deletion is atomic. Deploy version-2-capable instances with the flag off, enable it only after fleet compatibility is verified, and roll back by disabling it while retaining shared state for at least 30 minutes. Accepted verification criteria cover B1-B4, mixed-version operation, cutover, rollback, and preserved cookie semantics. Current evidence at s800 confirms the session API, application service, shared-store adapter, and deployment configuration boundaries and reports no drift.
evals.expected_output: A draft change specification that stops before implementation planning despite the request for planning artifacts.
assertions: The result is a Draft specification and requests explicit review or acceptance.
It emits no file-by-file tasks, shell commands, estimates, assignees, or implementation plan.
Any ordering is expressed only as a migration, compatibility, recovery, or verification constraint or a high-level slice dependency.
The response states that tactical planning begins only after the specification is explicitly accepted.
